bio: Chiu Yu Ko (高超禹) is an Associate Professor in the Department of Decisions, Operations and Technology at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) Business School. He also holds a courtesy appointment as Associate Professor in the Department of Economics, and serves as Associate Director of the Master of Science Programme in Information and Technology Management (MSc in ITM) as well as Associate Director of the Aviation Policy Research Centre.

He obtained his B.B.A. in Insurance, Financial and Actuarial Analysis (2005) and M.Phil. in Economics (2007) from The Chinese University of Hong Kong. He earned his M.A. in Economics (2009) and Ph.D. in Economics (2012) from Boston College. Upon graduation, he served as an assistant professor in the Department of Economics at the National University of Singapore (NUS) from 2012 to 2020 before joining CUHK.

His research focuses on game theory, industrial organization, political economy, and financial economics. In game theory, he works on bargaining, principal-agent problems, conflict resolution, and dynamic resource allocation. In industrial organization, he specializes in innovation, standard-setting (FRAND), platform competition, and patent licensing. In political economy, his work explores political centralization, state capacity, and comparative economic history. His research has been published in premier international journals including Management Science, Journal of Economic Theory, International Economic Review, Games and Economic Behavior, Journal of Environmental Economics and Management, Economic Inquiry, Economic Modelling, and Journal of Economics & Management Strategy.

He subscribes to the philosophy that effective learning requires understanding multiple facets in both depth and breadth. He believes continuous feedback allows students to learn from mistakes, consolidate acquired knowledge, and explore deeper academic and practical frontiers.

books.title: Technical Analysis with R
books.subtitle: An introductory textbook on testing technical trading strategies
books.description: An introductory textbook focusing on how to use R to test technical trading strategies. No prior programming knowledge is needed. Readers learn data manipulation (dplyr), econometric analysis (regression, time series), financial plotting (ggplot2, dygraphs), web scraping (rvest, wbstat, quantmod), and algorithmic strategy backtesting (quantstrat) with comprehensive performance evaluation.

books.title: TikZ Cookbook
books.subtitle: A 629-page comprehensive guide for drawing diagrams in economics
books.description: TikZ is a powerful drawing package in LaTeX. While it creates publication-quality vector diagrams, the learning curve can be steep. This 629-page cookbook provides step-by-step illustrations on using TikZ to draw various economic models, supply-demand shifts, game trees, pay-off matrices, and network graphs.

books.title: TikZ Cookbook Companion
books.subtitle: 100 Principles of Economics diagrams ready to use
books.description: A companion textbook with 100 diagrams commonly found in introductory and intermediate economics courses (Microeconomics, Macroeconomics, International Trade). Includes source code and explanations for quick diagram compilation.

publications.title: How would a monopsony employer hurt labor? A simple dynamic model
publications.abstract: This paper develops a dynamic model to investigate the mechanisms through which an employer with monopsony power adversely affects workers. We examine how imperfect competition in the labor market interacts with wage-setting dynamics, labor mobility, and long-term contract formation, demonstrating the welfare loss imposed on workers and offering policy insights regarding minimum wages and labor market concentration.

publications.title: Sharing Sequentially Triggered Losses: Automated Conflict Resolution Through Smart Contracts
publications.abstract: We consider a model of conflict resolution where an initial loss can trigger further losses along an acyclic network. Agents have committed in advance to an automated conflict resolution protocol using smart contracts. We study how to allocate such sequentially triggered losses among involved parties in an incentive-compatible, fair, and decentralized way, providing an axiomatic characterization and practical blockchain implementation principles.

publications.title: Sleeplessness, distraction and stock market performance: Evidence from the world cup
publications.abstract: We investigate how aggregate psychological distractions and sleep disruptions influence financial asset valuation by utilizing the FIFA World Cup as a natural experiment across international markets. Our empirical findings show that late-night viewing schedules cause measurable decreases in market liquidity and short-term mispricing, underscoring behavioral determinants of trading conduct.

publications.title: Can corruption encourage clean technology transfer?
publications.abstract: We examine the impact of bureaucratic corruption on the transfer of clean technology to developing economies. While corruption is widely recognized as a tax on economic activity and welfare, we demonstrate that when environmental regulations create rigid compliance barriers, intermediary rent-seeking may ironically provide strategic lubrication that facilitates the adoption of energy-saving technologies under specific market conditions, highlighting subtle trade-offs between regulatory rigor and environmental policy enforcement.

publications.title: A conceptual model for FRAND royalty setting
publications.abstract: Setting an industry-wide standard is crucial for the interoperability, compatibility, and efficiency of information and communication technologies. To minimize holdup problems, patent holders are often required to ex-ante commit to licensing their technologies under Fair, Reasonable, and Non-Discriminatory (FRAND) terms. Yet, there is little consensus, in both courtrooms and industries, on the exact meaning of FRAND. We propose a new framework that enables a precise distinction: fairness in the distribution of royalty payments among patent users, and reasonableness in setting the size of the compensation to the patent holder, where both the size and the distribution of payments are determined in a non-discriminatory way that ensures similar firms are treated similarly.

publications.title: Partial compatibility in two-sided markets: Equilibrium and welfare analysis
publications.abstract: This paper studies platform compatibility choices in two-sided markets where consumers and developers have heterogeneous preferences across competing systems. We model partial compatibility as a continuous design parameter and solve for subgame perfect equilibrium pricing and compatibility decisions, uncovering how multihoming tendencies govern whether proprietary walled gardens or open standards optimize overall economic surplus.

publications.title: Does licensing improve welfare with rent dissipation?
publications.abstract: When downstream patent licensees engage in unproductive contest activities that dissipate economic rents, patent licensing structures undergo fundamental strategic alterations. We analyze royalty and fixed-fee combinations that align licensor incentives with social efficiency, characterizing when rent dissipation causes standard open licensing policies to suboptimally restrict consumer surplus.

publications.title: Competitive screening and information transmission
publications.abstract: This paper studies competing uninformed principals screening privately informed agents who simultaneously convey verifiable signals. We demonstrate how decentralized competition alters signaling equilibrium structure compared to monolithic monopolistic mechanisms, highlighting implications for public credentialing and regulatory oversight.

publications.title: Are dominant platforms good for consumers?
publications.abstract: We examine whether dominant platforms inherently degrade consumer welfare when cross-side network externalities are strong. In contrast to conventional antitrust presumption against platform scale, our model identifies conditions under which platform asymmetry leads to larger network participation benefits that exceed monopolistic markup losses, delivering net consumer gains.

publications.title: Research Joint Venture with Technology Transfer
publications.abstract: This paper models an RJV where research partners are legally permitted to license newly generated innovations to outside rival firms. We demonstrate that allowing post-innovation technology transfer fundamentally improves initial R&D expenditure incentives, enhancing social welfare and softening competitive distortions in downstream product markets.

publications.title: Decentralized One-to-Many Bargaining
publications.abstract: We study decentralized bilateral bargaining between one central agent and multiple peripheral agents under alternative informational regimes. We characterize the unique stationary subgame perfect equilibrium and prove that delay vanishes as friction approaches zero. We analyze how outside options, bargaining power, and sequence of interactions determine division of surplus in decentralized supply chains and labor markets.

publications.title: Choosing a production joint venture partner
publications.venue: Journal of Institutional and Theoretical Economics, 176(4), 665–685
publications.abstract: Firms contemplating joint ventures often face asymmetric candidate partners with complementary capabilities and competing proprietary product lines. We formulate a non-cooperative partnership selection game to characterize equilibrium partner choice, showing how spillover risks and product substitutability interact with equity share allocations.

publications.title: Hide and Seek: Uninformed Traders and the Short-sales Constraints
publications.abstract: This paper studies the impact of short-sales constraints on market efficiency and informational friction in the presence of uninformed and informed traders. We show how constraints distort price discovery and the strategic behavior of traders in equity markets.

publications.title: Decentralized mechanisms for river sharing
publications.venue: Journal of Environmental Economics and Management, 94, 67–81
publications.abstract: Riparian nations situated along an international river face severe unidirectional externalities in water consumption. We design decentralized, voluntary bargaining mechanisms that implement Pareto-efficient water withdrawals without requiring a central supra-national authority, guaranteeing core stability and historical equity criteria.

publications.title: Unified China and Divided Europe
publications.abstract: Why did China historically maintain political unification while Europe remained fragmented into competitive sovereign states? We construct a formal geographical-defense model demonstrating how unidirectional external threats from Eurasian nomads compelled fiscal and administrative centralization in China, whereas multi-directional threats across Europe stabilized polycentric geopolitical competition.

publications.title: Sharing sequential values in a network
publications.abstract: We study the problem of sharing values generated sequentially across a directed network structure. When intermediate nodes contribute heterogeneous processing costs and pass-through capacity, standard cooperative solution concepts such as the Shapley value may fail monotonicity or incentive feasibility. We formulate an axiomatic foundation yielding unique, path-independent sharing rules suitable for supply networks, pipeline transport, and digital content distribution.

publications.title: On the role of outside options in wage renegotiation
publications.abstract: We investigate continuous labor renegotiation games when workers and employers possess time-varying outside opportunities. We find that outside options exert a discontinuous disciplinary role on wage agreements, explaining empirical stickiness in contractual adjustments during economic downturns.

publications.title: A note on budget constraints and outside options in common agency
publications.abstract: This paper analyzes the interplay between principal budget constraints and agent outside options in common agency games with complete information. I establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of pure-strategy equilibria and explore implications for political lobbying and multi-sponsor procurement.

publications.title: Regional dependence and political centralization in imperial China
publications.abstract: We explore the geographic and ecological determinants of administrative centralization across imperial Chinese dynasties. Inter-regional grain transfers and hydraulic infrastructure management generated high mutual dependence among provinces, sustaining unified dynastic governance even through acute political crises.

publications.title: Choosing a licensee from heterogeneous rivals
publications.abstract: A patent holder decides which rival firm in an oligopolistic industry should receive an exclusive cost-reducing production license. Because firms possess asymmetric initial cost efficiencies, licensing to a less efficient rival can strategically induce milder price competition in the final product market, altering traditional antitrust expectations.

publications.title: Profit-maximizing matchmaker
publications.abstract: We analyze a monopolistic matchmaker operating in two-sided matching markets with transferable utility. The intermediary posts registration fees and matching fees to attract participants. We characterize optimal tariff structures that maximize intermediary revenue while satisfying stable matching requirements.

teaching.title: Microeconomic Theory
teaching.semesters: Fall 2021, Fall 2022, Fall 2023, Fall 2024, Fall 2025, Fall 2026
teaching.overview: Rigorous doctoral-level introduction to modern microeconomic theory and mathematical economics. Detailed study of consumer theory, producer theory, general equilibrium under uncertainty, non-cooperative game theory, and mechanism design.
topics: Static & dynamic games of complete/incomplete info

teaching.title: Statistical Analysis
teaching.overview: Advanced statistical foundations for business analytics and empirical decision making. Covering probability theory, estimation, hypothesis testing, multivariate regression, and predictive modeling.

teaching.title: Low Altitude Economics
teaching.overview: Explores the emerging economic paradigms of the low-altitude economy, including unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) logistics, urban air mobility (UAM), airspace resource allocation, regulatory economics, and commercial infrastructure.
topics: Urban air mobility (UAM) & drone logistics networks

teaching.title: Economics for Finance Practice
teaching.overview: The course covers micro- and macro-economics fundamental to finance practice. Topics include game theory and its application in finance, asymmetric information, asset markets, portfolio theory, and macroeconomic monetary policies.

teaching.title: Game Theory for Business Strategy
teaching.overview: Applies non-cooperative and cooperative game theory to managerial decision-making and strategic competition. Covers dynamic price competition, entry deterrence, auction and mechanism design, platform ecosystems, and strategic bargaining.

teaching.title: Statistical Analysis for Business Decision
teaching.overview: Introductory and intermediate statistics for undergraduate business students. Practical applications using statistical computing and data analysis to solve complex managerial decisions.

teaching.title: STudent-oriented Teaching and Seminar
teaching.overview: Interactive, student-centered research seminar exploring real-world economic issues, analytical methodology, and project presentations.

teaching.title: Applied Financial Economics
teaching.overview: Equips students with analytical tools to understand security price movements and market microstructure. Covers fundamental analysis, technical trading, investor behavior, and quantitative financial econometrics.
topics: Technical trading & econometric backtesting in R

teaching.title: Financial Market Microstructure
teaching.semesters: Fall 2015, Fall 2016, Fall 2017, Spring 2017, Fall 2018, Spring 2019, Fall 2019
teaching.overview: Market microstructure studies price formation and the mechanics of trading in electronic markets. Investigates inventory models, sequential trade models, strategic trader behavior, and limit order book dynamics.

teaching.title: Industrial Organization
teaching.overview: Advanced doctoral field course in industrial organization covering monopoly behavior, oligopolistic competition, vertical relationships, network goods, two-sided platforms, and patent licensing.
